extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and academic peer reviewers invited to review manuscripts for Sage journals
extracted.subtask_description: Ethical standards and reviewer responsibilities for performing peer review of manuscripts submitted to Sage journals, including conflict disclosure, confidentiality, and how to handle suspected malpractice. Intended to guide reviewers on conduct, reporting concerns, and co-reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to COPE Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: We encourage our authors, editors, and reviewers to refer to the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) website. COPE has published a set of Guidelines for Peer Reviewers that we recommend reading prior to beginning a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult COPE's Guidelines for Peer Reviewers as foundational ethical guidance before starting a review; Sage also provides a video tutorial on peer review ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Please carefully consider whether you have any potential conflicts of interest relating to the paper before undertaking the review. As an example, you should not be reviewing papers written by anyone you have worked with, taught, and/or published work with in the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight any potential conflicts of interest to the journal editor as discreetly and as quickly as possible. Keep your reviewer account affiliation up to date so editors can identify potential conflicts prior to inviting you to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality of manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review process is confidential. You must not make personal use of unpublished information or communicate the content of manuscripts to others without the prior agreement of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep information about any potential ethical concerns confidential; consult the editor (do not discuss concerns with anyone other than the journal editor). Do not use unpublished data or ideas for your own purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact authors directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not contact the authors directly without the permission of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any communication with authors should be routed via or permitted by the journal/editor to preserve confidentiality and the integrity of the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bias—judge only on research quality and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please be careful not to make judgements about the paper based on personal, financial, intellectual biases or any considerations other than the quality of the research and written presentation of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manuscripts on methodological rigour, validity, and clarity rather than outcomes, authors' identities, affiliations, or your own preferences or financial interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report discovery of author identity in double-anonymized review
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are reviewing for a journal that uses double-anonymized peer review and come to discover the identity of the author through any means (such as reading a preprint or seeing a paper presented at a conference), please inform the journal editor immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to unmask authors deliberately; if identity is discovered incidentally, notify the editor so they can decide on next steps or reassign the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain permission before involving junior researchers / co-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes you may want to involve junior researchers in the review of an article, or a senior colleague may ask you to contribute. In either case, please ensure that you obtain permission from the journal editor prior to completing the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supervisor must agree to provide guidance during the review process and approve the final review. Note the names of those who contributed to the review in the 'Confidential Comments to the Editor' box when submitting your review. See Web of Science Reviewer Recognition for recognition options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not suggest citations to benefit your own citation count
rubrics_metrics.description: As per COPE guidelines, reviewers should not suggest that authors include citations of the reviewer’s work merely to increase their citation count or to enhance the visibility of their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any suggested citations must be based on valid academic or technological reasons directly relevant to the manuscript; self-serving citation requests are unethical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not penalize research for non-positive or null outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of non-positive outcomes should not influence your assessment of the quality of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methodological quality, transparency, and appropriateness of analysis irrespective of whether results are positive, negative, or null.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep reviewer profile/affiliation up to date
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep your affiliation up to date on your reviewer account, so that editors can easily identify if you have a conflict of interest with the authors of a manuscript before inviting you to review the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate affiliation and profile information enables editors to manage conflicts and make informed reviewer selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify editor if you suspect duplicate submission or prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact the journal editor to discuss the situation without delay if you suspect that the paper has been either published or submitted to another journal. The author should disclose any prior distribution and/or publication of any portion of the material to the Editor for their consideration and ensure that appropriate attribution is included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not independently pursue or investigate beyond informing the editor; let the editorial office handle verification and follow-up with the author(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify editor if you suspect plagiarism or copyright infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: You suspect that the paper plagiarizes the work of others. Sage takes issues of copyright infringement, plagiarism, and other breaches of best practice very seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report suspected plagiarism to the editor promptly. Sage will investigate claims of plagiarism or misuse of published articles to protect authors' rights and the journal's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected problems with research ethics (permissions, COIs, funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: You suspect that there might be problems with the ethics of the research conducted. It is the responsibility of the authors to disclose any potential conflicts of interest as well as any funding bodies that have contributed to facilitating the research. It is also the responsibility of the authors to ensure that they have the necessary permissions for any use of data or results sourced from others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have concerns about ethical approval, participant consent, data permissions, undisclosed funding or COIs, contact the editor without delay and refer to Sage's Publication ethics policies (Conflict of interest policy, Funding acknowledgements policy, and other policies) for further guidance.
